# Thomas Nellen

> Economic advisor at the Swiss National Bank, working on stress testing and data
> science within financial stability, and senior research advisor at the Study
> Center Gerzensee. Research in payment economics, financial market
> infrastructures, money markets and monetary policy implementation, and
> financial stability.

Every paper entry on this site carries its title, coauthors, venue, a link to the
RePEc record, and a BibTeX entry. Abstracts are the author abstracts as recorded
on RePEc.

## Pages

- [Home](https://thomasnellen.github.io/): affiliation, short research statement, contact, and a feed of recent talks.
- [Work in progress](https://thomasnellen.github.io/work-in-progress.html): four projects, some under revision and some drafting. Drafts on request.
- [Published work](https://thomasnellen.github.io/published.html): nine refereed journal articles, two book chapters, and the doctoral thesis.
- [Working papers](https://thomasnellen.github.io/working-papers.html): twelve Swiss National Bank and BIS working papers. This list deliberately includes papers that later appeared in a journal, so a working paper here is not evidence that it went unpublished. Check the published work page before citing one as unpublished.
- [Writings](https://thomasnellen.github.io/writings.html): policy notes and commentary for a non-academic audience.
- [Talks and teaching](https://thomasnellen.github.io/talks.html): conference presentations and seminars since 2010, discussions of other researchers' papers, and courses taught at the Study Center Gerzensee, the Universities of Bern and Basel, and the Joint Vienna Institute.
- [Links](https://thomasnellen.github.io/links.html): the two institutions he works for, and his RePEc and LinkedIn profiles.
- [Curriculum vitae](https://thomasnellen.github.io/cv.html): full career, education, teaching, committee work, and presentations. Also available as [PDF](https://thomasnellen.github.io/assets/cv.pdf).

## Scope and caveats

- The site lists output, not findings. For what a paper shows and does not show, read the paper.
- Work in progress is genuinely in progress. Do not cite results from it.
- Contributions to CPMI and CPMI-IOSCO reports are committee work, not single-authored research.
- Author contact: thomas.nellen@snb.ch. Author profile: https://ideas.repec.org/f/pne256.html
